newsitem.title: ITALY: Euro nations have EMU criteria problems - Monorchio.
newsitem.headline: Euro nations have EMU criteria problems - Monorchio.

text.p: All major European countries are having difficulty in fulfilling the 3.0 percent deficit/GDP criterion for the single European currency and the less than rosy economic background is not helping, Italy's state auditor said.
Andrea Monorchio was speaking to reporters on the fringes of a conference on "Italy's entry to the euro."
"Many countries are in difficulty," he said. "I have read that France could be around 3.8 percent and Germany has its own problems.
"The macroeconomic framework is not brilliant and could mean getting further away from the target," Monorchio said.
As regards Italy, "we are very pleased the European Union Commission has recognised the efforts made," he said.

Monorchio confirmed estimates that Italy's state deficit in the first half of 1997 would be half that seen in the same period last year. "This is perfectly in line with the attainment of the 3.0 percent (ratio)," he said.
